original_question: Let Gamma be a nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = 5. Is it always true that the type t(Gamma) is at most 5, and is equality possible only when Gamma is almost symmetric?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 20 ([MS21, Question 4.2]) of arXiv:2406.00790, in the subsection on almost symmetric and nearly Gorenstein semigroups.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem essentially verbatim: it has the right class of objects (nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups), the correct hypothesis on embedding dimension (edim(Γ)=5), the precise proposed bound on the type (t(Γ)≤5), and the correct extremal clause that equality should occur only in the almost symmetric case.
missing_details: It should define a numerical semigroup as a cofinite additive submonoid of ℕ.
It should make explicit that edim(Γ) is the number of minimal generators of Γ.
It should define the pseudo-Frobenius set PF(Γ) and the type t(Γ)=|PF(Γ)|.
It should define the Frobenius number Frob(Γ)=max PF(Γ), since this appears in the definition of almost symmetric.
It should spell out the nearly Gorenstein condition used in the paper: if Γ=⟨g1,…,g5⟩, then for each minimal generator gi there exists pi∈PF(Γ) such that gi+pi−q∈Γ for every q∈PF(Γ).
It should define almost symmetric exactly: for every x∈ℤ\Γ, either Frob(Γ)-x∈Γ or both x and Frob(Γ)-x belong to PF(Γ).
It should make the universal quantifier explicit: the question asks whether this holds for every nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup with five minimal generators.
It should clarify that 'equality' means the extremal case t(Γ)=5.
refined_question: Let Γ⊆ℕ be a numerical semigroup, that is, a cofinite additive submonoid, with minimal generators g1<⋯<g5, so that edim(Γ)=5. Let PF(Γ)={p∈ℤ\Γ : p+γ∈Γ for all γ∈Γ\{0}} be its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, let t(Γ)=|PF(Γ)| be its type, and let Frob(Γ)=max PF(Γ). Assume that Γ is nearly Gorenstein, meaning that for each i∈{1,…,5} there exists pi∈PF(Γ) such that gi+pi−q∈Γ for every q∈PF(Γ). Must one have t(Γ)≤5? Moreover, if t(Γ)=5, must Γ be almost symmetric, i.e. must it satisfy that for every x∈ℤ\Γ, either Frob(Γ)-x∈Γ or both x and Frob(Γ)-x belong to PF(Γ)?
justification: The draft is already a very close paraphrase of the paper’s exact target: Section 5 states Problem 20 in essentially the same words. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the nearby context, one must import the notation fixed earlier in Section 1 (embedding dimension, pseudo-Frobenius numbers, type, Frobenius number) and the definitions given immediately before Problem 20 for almost symmetric and nearly Gorenstein semigroups. The nearby Theorem 15 gives the proven four-generator case t(Γ)≤3 for nearly Gorenstein semigroups, showing that Problem 20 is precisely the next sharp five-generator question. No ambient field, grading, homogeneity, or ring-theoretic hypothesis is part of the statement itself; the problem is formulated purely at the semigroup level.
